points.text: No ablation of synthesis components (tactic constraint, pruning, budget decay, continuing after proof).
No comparison with data from ordinary tree search using the same seeds and policy.
No data-scaling curve despite title/abstract claims about scalable large-scale data.
Gains confounded by extra STP/Mathlib data and BFS-Prover as exploration policy (distillation).
Search budgets differ between proposed method and baselines despite 'same budget' claim.
Baselines evaluated at a single beam size while own model gets several plus adaptive.
Beam sizes and adaptive hyperparameters chosen on test sets; no validation split.
Claim of no beam-size search contradicted by per-benchmark adaptive parameters.
Gains small relative to variance; '±' undefined, number of runs and seeds not stated.
ProofNet superiority over InternLM holds only at test-selected configurations.
Efficiency claims (overhead, early termination, DoBeVi runtime) have no cost measurements.
Figure 3 cross-reference in Section 3.2 points to wrong figure.
Notation mixes 'tactic' and 'proof step'.
Claim that beam size 2 gives larger variance contradicted by reported ±.
Related work omits HunyuanProver, closest data-synthesis plus tree-search system.
Data recipe not differentiated from transition data of prior EI provers; novelty asserted.
'No EI' framing hides that exploration policy and seeds are EI products; distils baseline.
Baseline numbers far below published larger-budget results; SOTA claim holds only at restricted budget.
Adaptive beam not situated against known schedules; no alternative schedule baselines.
Title/abstract claim scaling results; experiments are a single table.
No ablation removing data or search contributions to attribute gains.
No validation split used.
'±' undefined and number of runs not stated.
No dataset release statement for the 20M-transition set.
Budget notation for adaptive row omits beam size.
Table 1 mixes imported and re-evaluated numbers within rows.
Figure 3 cross-reference in Section 3.2 is wrong.
'Tactic'/'proof step' notation drift.
Grammar errors in Section 1 and Figure 3 caption.
Beam sizes and adaptive parameters selected on test; ProofNet superiority only at selected config.
Teacher-student confound: BFS-Prover exploration policy plus extra data, compared to BFS-Prover.
Baselines run with unequal budgets and beams.
Title claim that performance hinges on scalable data is untested.
SOTA claim true only at restricted budget; published baseline results higher.
Computational overhead and early-termination claims lack numbers.
Data-distribution explanation of beam-size optima is untested speculation.
Inconsistent statements on decoupling tactic and premise generation.
BLEU decontamination threshold unstated and BLEU a weak duplicate detector.
Scoring function calibration under diversified exploration data unexamined.
Adaptive schedule shape under-described; beam hits floor early.
Mean beam, total tactic samples and wall-clock per problem not reported.
Pass@1 here implies hundreds of Lean calls, unlike whole-proof pass@1.
Timeout rate per configuration not reported.
No harder or out-of-distribution benchmark to probe seed dependence.
No comparison with alternative schedules like progressive widening or diverse beam search.
No broader-impact paragraph.
Abstract phrase about proof-state exploration is vague.
Motivation in Section 1 is disjointed.
Figure 1 uses unexplained tactics; unhelpful for general audience.
Algorithm 1 notation inconsistent and mixes implementation details.
No comparison with whole-proof generation methods.
No ablation separating data synthesis from adaptive beam size.
No analysis of which problem types benefit most.
Scoring function acknowledged flawed but no fix or alternative offered.
Multiple exploration strategies (MCTS, length-normalized BFS, top-p) failed.
No ablation on size of the 60-tactic set.
No ablation on pruning parameters alpha, beta, gamma.
Base model zero-shot results missing; baselines not fine-tuned from same base.
Synthetic data not evaluated under standard search; exploration contribution not ablated.
No algorithmic comparison of new tree search with existing approaches.
BFS-Prover not evaluated with larger compute budget.
Pruning and beam-decay hyperparameters fixed ad hoc without sensitivity analysis.
Methodology lacks intuition for constrained decoding and parameter choices.
Log-prob scoring admitted suboptimal but no quantitative failure analysis.
Exploration bounded to seed neighborhoods; out-of-distribution generalization concerns.

P.summary: No ablation of synthesis components or of data vs search contributions.
No comparison with standard tree-search data from same seeds/policy.
Scaling claims in title/abstract untested; no data-scaling curve.
Gains confounded by BFS-Prover exploration policy, EI inheritance and extra data.
Unequal budgets and beam tuning between method and baselines.
Hyperparameters selected on test sets without validation split.
Variance undefined, runs unstated; gains within noise.
Efficiency claims not supported by cost measurements.
Adaptive schedule shape and per-problem compute not reported.
Wrong Figure 3 cross-reference.
Tactic/proof step notation drift.
Beam-2 variance claim contradicted by table.
Missing HunyuanProver and differentiation from prior EI data pipelines; novelty unestablished.
SOTA claim only holds at restricted budget; published numbers higher.
Adaptive beam not compared to known alternative search schedules.
No dataset release statement.
Adaptive row budget notation omits B.
Table mixes imported and re-evaluated numbers.
Grammar errors.
Speculative explanation of beam-size optima.
Inconsistent statements on tactic/premise decoupling.
Decontamination via BLEU underspecified and weak.
Scoring function calibration with diversified data unexamined.
Pass@1 semantics differ from whole-proof regime.
Timeout rate not reported.
No out-of-distribution evaluation for seed dependence.
No broader-impact statement.

Q.summary: No comparison with whole-proof generation methods.
No ablation isolating data synthesis vs adaptive beam/exploration.
No analysis of which problems benefit.
Scoring function flawed without fix or failure analysis.
No sensitivity analysis for pruning/decay hyperparameters.
Base model performance missing; baselines not on same base.
No algorithmic comparison with existing tree-search approaches.
BFS-Prover not tested with larger compute budget.
Exploration limited to seed neighborhoods; OOD generalization.
